cause: Context Pack was frozen before development started.
impact: The line has an evidence-bound starting context.
lesson: Freeze the initial context before changing implementation state.

cause: User asked that the v1.6.2 external review and the v1.8.11 post-release self-check be planned in the v1.8.12 handoff, with every item owned even when it is not done in v1.8.12.
impact: The kickoff handoff now holds the single owner table (version and completion standard per item: v1.8.12 step, v1.8.13, v1.9.0, or trigger condition). Objective step 3 also commits the pre-push guard source, installer and tests. Context Pack objective text predates this addition; the objective file and this event are authoritative.
lesson: Plan follow-ups with an owner and a completion standard at the moment they are found, not at the next release.

cause: Three GET routes and one lazily created lock wrote to disk on read: notebook options appended a context.compiled trace event per view, unknown agent-session and column-cast record lookups created empty storage directories, and the first preference read created its flock file.
impact: Any page may issue a GET, and only state-changing methods are held to the Origin check, so a GET that writes is a cross-site write path. Notebook options moved to POST (provenance kept), lookups no longer create storage, the lock file is created at startup. One accepted exception: marking a dead running run as interrupted.
lesson: Enumerate every registered GET route against a real project and fail on any file created or modified; new routes are then covered automatically.

cause: Vite 5.4.21 answers CORS for any localhost origin, including on its /api proxy, and forwards the browser Origin unchanged; a page on another local port could therefore read proxied backend responses. The objective only required the Origin check on state-changing methods.
impact: Origin, when present, is now checked for every method. Browser probe D from a :9999 page through the Vite proxy received the 403 body instead of the LLM config. Same-origin UI reads carry no Origin and are unaffected. Also: an allowed loopback origin now covers the other loopback names on the same port, after the UI opened as localhost was refused with only 127.0.0.1 configured.
lesson: When a dev proxy sits in front of a local API, test the hostile page through the proxy as well as directly; the proxy's own CORS policy can turn a write-only defence into a read leak.

cause: Five cases in tests/eval_v1811 retained evaluation scripts (not in default collection) fail on the baseline 3a96c19a as well as with the step-1 change: three in glm_nb_public_review_first_source/adversarial and two in count_public_review_adversarial; one reports a changed source artifact fingerprint.
impact: No step-1 regression; the evaluation scripts are not part of the default suite. Owned by objective step 3, which moves evaluation scripts out of the tests collection surface; decide there whether they are repaired or archived as evidence.
lesson: Baseline every failure on the unchanged commit before attributing it to the current change.

cause: Objective step 1 acceptance: browser UI through the Vite proxy, a foreign-origin page, a forged Host, and a no-Origin client.
impact: Passed. UI on :5192 completed create project, upload, OLS fit, Agent Wald post-estimation, Stata script export and Notebook load with no refusal. Seven foreign-page attempts (fetch, no-cors, multipart and urlencoded forms, direct and via the Vite proxy) were all refused with nothing created; forged Host refused; curl without Origin unaffected. Worktree Vite servers on non-default ports now need WORKBENCH_ALLOWED_ORIGINS on the backend.
lesson: Accept a local-security change with a real hostile page on another port, not only with unit tests.

cause: The first version of the 'importing a test module creates nothing' test redirected the evidence store to a temporary root and asserted that root stayed empty; the old code wrote to the real local/ path instead, so the assertion passed against unfixed code.
impact: Caught before implementation was trusted: the test now also snapshots the real local/ tree, failed against the old code, and passes after the fix.
lesson: A negative assertion (nothing was written) must observe the location the unfixed code actually writes to; confirm it fails before the fix.

cause: Objective step 2 acceptance: run the evidence-writing tests repeatedly and confirm local/ stays bounded.
impact: Passed. Five consecutive script-export runs cap each category at 3 runs; a failed run survives four later passing runs; LMM admission keeps nothing on success, keeps with .keep on request and with .failed on an injected failure. Pruning is confined to local/test-evidence; older local/v1811-* evidence is untouched and moves with step 3.
lesson: Bound test evidence by category and run, never by deleting outside a dedicated managed root.

cause: The five tests/eval_v1811 review cases are pinned to their manifest commits. Re-run at 67088c98 and compared with the recorded outputs: two assert GLM-NB has no live evaluation and two assert GLM-NB post-estimation is closed, both later changed on purpose in v1.8.11; one is the reviewer's first-version snapshot whose recorded first run already failed.
impact: No product regression. The frozen review scripts stay in place outside default collection; the evidence policy states they are not maintained. Closes the open GAP recorded in step 1.
lesson: Review scripts pinned to a commit must say so in a policy, or a later reader treats their failures as regressions.

cause: Objective step 3 acceptance: the size guard names oversized additions, and the installed pre-push guard refuses private refs and license values while allowing normal pushes.
impact: Passed. Staging a 2 MiB file and a new file in a frozen evaluation root made the guard exit 1 naming both paths; the branch is within budget since v1.8.11. Thirteen real-push cases pass in a temporary repository; the versioned hook is byte-identical to the one installed in the main checkout.
lesson: Calibrate a repository budget on past versions and make it name the offending paths, so it blocks the outlier without blocking normal work.

cause: Objective step 4 acceptance: generated frontend API types with a drift test.
impact: 133/133 operations declare their success response; 127/128 JSON operations validated strictly against real responses in the HTTP suite (1461 tests); frontend client functions returning hand-written server shapes 66 -> 0 (compiler-level invariant); tsc clean, vitest 1778 pass; drift demo (renamed GraphStats.leaf_count) fails the drift test and, regenerated, makes tsc name graphAdapter.ts:223; browser acceptance on 127.0.0.1:5192 with no console errors and all API requests 200.
lesson: Make the types modular at the source: derive response types from domain dataclasses/models and Literal value sets, enforce them in tests, and judge frontend provenance with the compiler instead of a list of names.

cause: The statistical exploration HTTP request listed six operations in its own Literal; the engine's OPERATIONS and the UI's Frequencies option used a seventh (tabulate).
impact: Choosing Frequencies in the graph's statistical exploration returned 422 since tabulate was added. Fixed with one ExplorationOperation Literal that the engine, the request model and the frontend read; route test asserts the request accepts every engine operation; browser preview returns 200.
lesson: A value set has one definition; validators, request models and UI read it. Two hand lists drift silently.

cause: Strict response validation only sees the responses tests produce. No HTTP test returned a non-empty memory retrieval, a figure without its source, or summarize_detail/misstable/corr/grouped explorations.
impact: Two wrong declarations passed validation (memory_source as text; figure source never null). Tests were added for each branch and the declarations corrected; 127/128 JSON operations are now exercised.
lesson: For every declared union branch or optional value, add the HTTP test that produces it; contract coverage is measured per branch, not per route.

cause: Prediction evidence structure was tightened earlier in step 4 and checked only with a filtered test selection; frequency-weighted runs add provenance.
impact: A contract violation reached the branch until the full HTTP run caught it; fixed with StructureKind/StructureProvenance shared by StructureSpecV1.
lesson: After tightening a response type, run the full contract suite, not a keyword-filtered subset.

cause: The graph's control registry listed kinds the backend never sends (radio/slider/textarea) and lacked column/integer/number/object/json, which fell through to a read-only placeholder.
impact: Ordinal/multinomial logit, Cox, LMM, quantile regression, ARMA-GARCH and ETS parameters of those kinds cannot be edited in the graph operation panel. Kinds now come from the generated ControlKind; behavior unchanged; in-place editors deferred (BACKLOG V1812-GRAPH-CONTROL-KINDS, v1.9.0).
lesson: UI vocabularies of server kinds must be generated; a hand list hides missing renderers behind a fallback.

cause: Typing every operation exposed contracts with no producer or no reachable caller: notebook authorize-execution refuses bound options while its service requires them; node-level rerun_from is consumed but never produced.
impact: Both kept as is, recorded as BACKLOG V1812-NOTEBOOK-AUTHORIZE and V1812-NODE-RERUN-FROM for a keep-or-remove decision; dead reads (editable_schema_version, sizeBytes) removed.
lesson: Declaring a type for each operation is also an inventory: an operation no test can reach or a field no producer writes is a decision to make, not a type to write.

cause: User reviewed the three step-4 GAPs and the repository file budget.
impact: Graph in-place editing of column/integer/number/object/json controls goes to v1.9.0 (BACKLOG V1812-GRAPH-CONTROL-KINDS). Node-level rerun provenance: implement if necessary, without simplifying (done). Notebook authorize-execution: decide by the Notebook's purpose; recommendation pending user confirmation. 512 KiB per-file budget: set by the assistant in step 3, explanation and options pending user decision.
lesson: Present each open GAP with the owner's original intent and a recommendation; a removal needs the user's word even when it is the recommendation.

cause: v1.6.3 specified run-level and node-level rerun_from; only run-level was written, so Compare with source relied on a read-time fallback that fails closed for nodes shared by several runs.
impact: Node-level provenance is persisted with the produced node, settled across runs (conflicts fail closed), consumed by the frontend gate, and the decision is recorded in resolver_trace. Browser: a confirmed rerun's model node offers Compare with source from node-level provenance.
lesson: When a spec names a source of truth and a transitional fallback, track the source of truth to completion; a fallback that works in the common case hides that it was never built.

cause: run_inputs.rerun_from was written in three shapes (context rerun provenance, context-less Agent rerun record, data-operation dataset bridge); script export read every one as a dataset bridge.
impact: Script export failed on every rerun child with a leaked KeyError ('source_run_id', 422); the forest served bridges and partial records as provenance against its declared type. Fixed: rerun_from is provenance only, dataset_source is the bridge, readers validate shape and read legacy bridges; rerun children whose upload equals the parent's export from the parent's source.
lesson: One key carries one contract; a second meaning gets its own field and a typed reader, or every consumer guesses which shape it got.

cause: User approved listing the generated frontend API types (430 KiB, near the 512 KiB per-file limit the assistant set in step 3) with a 1 MiB cap instead of raising the global limit.
impact: scripts/repo_evidence_allowlist.json lists frontend/src/generated/api-schema.ts with a reason and a 1 MiB cap; the budget check now reports exceptions for files no longer in the repository.
lesson: Budget generated code separately from evidence, by a named exception with its own cap, so the evidence limit keeps its meaning.

cause: User approved removing the Notebook authorize-execution route (2026-10-08): it accepted an envelope of execution authorizations supplied by the client, no input could succeed, and the Notebook flow (plan options, confirm one, server executes) needs only authorizations the server issues.
impact: Route, request model, response type and unused frontend function removed; NotebookService.authorize_option_execution kept for confirm-and-execute. Route test locks the route out. 1672 tests (HTTP, notebook, capability execution, authorize_option_execution callers), 1782 frontend tests and the browser Notebook view pass.
lesson: Before removing an entry point, inventory every reference and keep the internal operation other paths depend on; lock the removal with a test.

cause: workbench run declared about 40 options by hand and called orchestrator.run_workflow directly, bypassing the run service the HTTP route uses; model_options, the three weights, prediction data structure, statistical tests and by-group were missing, and run inputs and the analysis ledger differed from UI runs.
impact: One field table (run_request.py) now builds both the POST /runs signature and the CLI options; both submit through _submit_run. A test asserts the CLI and HTTP hand the workflow identical arguments. Post-estimation, export-script, export-targets and models subcommands are generated from the step contracts and catalog.
lesson: Declare a request once and generate every entry point from it; a second hand-written entry point drifts silently.

cause: The step-5 acceptance runs an NB1 export in Stata, but v1.8.11 validated native export only for estimated-dispersion NB2; NB1 fell back to a result sidecar, so Stata would replay Workbench numbers instead of re-estimating.
impact: NB1 now exports natively to Stata (nbreg with dispersion(constant)) and Python (statsmodels nb1), checked by model and Wald/lincom oracles executed in real Stata 18 MP and Python. R has no reference NB1 estimator and keeps the sidecar with a stated reason (V1812-NB1-R-EXPORT). Fixed alpha still requires Workbench.
lesson: When an acceptance says a script runs in Stata, require fully_native so a sidecar replay cannot pass for re-estimation.

cause: Generated commands were first built as click.Command objects; typer 0.26 ships its own vendored click, so click.exceptions.Exit raised by --help was not caught by Typer's main loop and --help exited 1.
impact: Commands are now built with Typer's public API from a generated inspect.Signature, the same approach as the route signature; no direct click import remains in the CLI.
lesson: Extend a Typer app only through Typer's public API; its click is private and its exception classes differ from the installed click.

cause: Objective step 5 acceptance: from the command line, negative binomial NB1, then Wald, then a Stata script export run natively in Stata.
impact: Passed. NB1 fit on 600 rows, Wald chi2(2) = 147.972; export fully_native with cleaning, NB1 and Wald all native; stata-mp batch run exit 0 with 19 self-checks passing and the same chi2 in the Stata log. CLI help 0.11 s against a 0.5 s budget. Evidence kept locally with the Stata log redacted; no raw log hash in tracked files. 1069 script-export, CLI, types, capability and post-estimation tests and 559 run-route tests pass.
lesson: Accept a CLI by running the whole chain as a user would, including the exported script in the target program from a cold start.

cause: The model-family contract table lived in agent/workflow_contracts.py and the JSONL helpers in agent/storage.py, so the engine (capabilities, estimation), orchestrator, admission, events and exploration_log imported the Agent layer: 12 upward imports, all function-level and therefore invisible to import-time checks.
impact: Family contracts and result shapes now live in contracts/model, OperationValidationError in contracts/common/errors, JSONL helpers in workbench/jsonl_store; every importer names the new module directly. A static guard over 13 lower packages and modules (function-level and relative imports resolved) fails on any import of workbench.agent.
lesson: Guard layering statically over the whole AST, including imports inside functions; lazy imports are where upward dependencies hide.

cause: Objective step 6 acceptance: a layering guard test that fails when a lower-layer module imports the Agent layer.
impact: Passed. Guard failed first with 12 upward imports and passes after the move; importing contracts.model.family, jsonl_store, events, exploration_log, admission, engine.capabilities or orchestrator alone loads no workbench.agent module. Full backend suite 8088 passed; its 4 failures (ratchet baseline, 3 subprocess import) fixed in the same commit and rechecked.
lesson: Run the full suite after a cross-package move; the failures it surfaces can be environmental faults the move only exposed.

cause: The shared virtualenv's editable install named the workbench-v1.8.6 worktree. Tests that started a Python subprocess without their own PYTHONPATH therefore imported v1.8.6 code; after that worktree was archived on 2026-10-07 they could not import workbench and three devline enforcement tests failed.
impact: tests/conftest.py puts this checkout's backend first on PYTHONPATH for every subprocess; a new test fails if a subprocess imports workbench from anywhere else. The shared virtualenv is left unchanged because every worktree shares it.
lesson: Subprocess tests must pin the import root to the checkout under test; a shared editable install silently tests another version.

cause: agent/notebook/vocabulary.py kept its own table of what each of 20 model families publishes, beside the family contracts that already declare each family's artifacts; a new family had to be added in both places.
impact: ModelFamilyContract.published_artifacts declares it per family (validated to the family's own artifacts); the vocabulary derives the table. A test pins the derived table to the previous one entry for entry. Family-literal ratchet 165 to 119 (26 contract declarations moved in step 6, 20 removed here).
lesson: When a consumer keeps a per-family table, move the fact onto the family contract and derive the table.

cause: The family-literal ratchet regex matches any quoted name ending in _1, so draft node ids such as model_1, table_1, source_1 and input_1 are counted as family names: 45 of the remaining 119.
impact: The measurement was left unchanged in this version so the reported drop stays comparable; true family-name branches are 74. Recorded in BACKLOG V1812-FAMILY-LITERAL-DOWN for v1.8.13: exclude node ids and rebaseline at 74 before further migration.
lesson: Do not change a ratchet's measurement in the same change that reports its drop; record the miscount and correct it separately.

cause: Objective step 7 acceptance: the family-literal ratchet baseline lowered from 165 to at most 145.
impact: Passed at 119. Notebook, Agent, LMM, survival, family-contract, workflow-contract and layering tests: 1236 passed; the one failure seen when run from backend/ is a cwd-relative fixture path and passes from the repository root as the gate runs it.
lesson: Report how much of a ratchet drop is relocation and how much is real removal.

cause: Formulas reference columns as Q(repr(column)), but seven backend readers and one frontend reader undid it by stripping quote characters, handling only the single-quoted form: names with both quotes or a backslash came back escaped, a quoted name containing a colon was split as an interaction, ANOVA built unescaped Q('name') and failed on a single quote, and the egress redactor did not recognise Q("o'brien") so a protected column's category level would be sent.
impact: workbench/formula_terms.py is the one implementation (ast.literal_eval of the literal); every reader and generator uses it, the frontend decodes the same escapes. 11 backend tests failed before the fix. The run pipeline normalises column names to [0-9a-z_] before estimation (checked on the main and data-node model entries), so the redaction gap was latent rather than reachable through normal runs.
lesson: Parse an encoded value with the decoder of the encoding that produced it, in one place; ad hoc quote stripping fails on the first escape.

cause: Switching MANOVA's generator to quote_column changed the formula text its result envelope records from JSON double quotes to repr single quotes; two MANOVA tests pin that text as the result contract and failed in the full suite.
impact: MANOVA keeps its JSON quoting; the shared reader accepts JSON-quoted names, now pinned by a test. The exported Python helper change is recorded as a reviewed correction in the sidecar snapshot test, leaving the reviewed snapshot unchanged.
lesson: Before unifying a generator, check whether its output is recorded in a published result; unify the reader instead of the recorded format.

cause: Objective step 8 acceptance (user scoped to V1811-PUBLIC-TERM-QUOTE): the item's own tests.
impact: Passed. 48 term tests (10 column names through every reader, egress redaction through the real send path, OLS and ANOVA fits), 15 frontend tests; backend full suite 8131 passed with its 3 failures handled; frontend 1797 passed. No browser scenario: runs normalise column names, so the UI cannot produce quoted terms.
lesson: Verify whether a defect is reachable through the product before describing its impact; report latent and live defects differently.

cause: Two self-review rounds after the first host gate: steps 5-8 code and the whole branch. Findings: README lacked the generated commands; the CLI wait re-subscribed without unsubscribing when a stream closed without a terminal event; export-script raised a bare StopIteration for an unregistered bundle; an undecodable Q() literal raised SyntaxError in the term readers and the egress redactor; a trailing blank line; kickoff owner rows for steps 1-4 not marked done.
impact: All fixed with tests in ab454009. The first egress fix still sent the level because it returned early without recording the redaction; the failing test caught it. Every kickoff owner row now has an owner and completion state.
lesson: Test every fail-closed branch of a redactor through the real send path; an early return can skip the bookkeeping that decides whether redaction happened.

cause: Host full gate launched from the terminal panel (user instruction 2026-10-08), with no Vite or uvicorn running, before and after the self-review fixes.
impact: Both passed. b305edf1: backend 8144 passed in 18:23, golden 23, frontend 1797, tsc clean, total 19:12. ab454009: backend 8148 passed in 18:17, golden 23, frontend 1797, tsc clean, total 23:28; the extra time is frontend environment startup (setup 267 s vs 5 s) under machine load, tests themselves unchanged.
lesson: Rerun the full gate on the exact commit to be released after any review fix that touches code.

cause: User authorized the release after both host gates and the two self-review rounds, and asked that the shared virtualenv install be repointed to the main checkout after the merge, without touching other worktrees, then the CLI acceptance be repeated with the real workbench command.
impact: v1.8.12 released: main squash 91550d73 (tree identical to the branch tip), annotated tag v1.8.12, GitHub Release https://github.com/damndone/Arboris/releases/tag/v1.8.12. scripts/install_dev_env.py repointed the editable install to the main checkout and installed the checkout hook; the release gate on 91550d73 passed including the new dev-environment stage (backend 8156 passed in 18:26); the real workbench command repeated NB1, Wald and the native Stata run outside any checkout; the v1.8.11 worktree, unchanged, imports its own code.
lesson: Archiving a worktree can break every checkout that shares a virtualenv naming it; check the shared install before removing a worktree and gate it.

cause: Every objective step is delivered and released; the earlier release event carried no state transition, so the line still reported STARTED.
impact: v1-8-12 line closed as COMPLETED after release; the retrospective is regenerated and, for a completed line, verified against the event log. Open follow-ups are owned in the kickoff table and BACKLOG (v1.8.13 and v1.9.0).
lesson: Close a version line with an explicit state transition; a release event without state_to leaves the line reported as started.
